arguments.value: Victor Marrero is a United States District Judge for the Southern District of New York, assuming senior status in 2010 after being appointed by President Bill Clinton in 1999. Born in Santurce, Puerto Rico, in 1941, he earned a B.A. from New York University and an LL.B. from Yale Law School. Before joining the federal bench, Marrero served in a range of public leadership roles in New York City and State, including in the Lindsay and Carey administrations, as chairman of the City Planning Commission, and as an undersecretary of housing and urban development. He later entered private practice and represented the United States internationally as ambassador to the U.N. Economic and Social Council and as permanent representative to the Organization of American States.
